claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially a high-temperature single-phase BCC alloy.
Cr diffuses faster or more favorably than the other constituent elements during cooling from the BCC state.
Differential diffusion during cooling produces local compositional fluctuations.
The compositional fluctuations consist of Cr-enriched regions correspondingly depleted in Co, Fe, and Ni.
Cr-enriched regions act as nucleation and growth sites for ordered secondary phases in the metastable BCC matrix.
Cr segregation lowers the nucleation barrier for ordered phases such as B2 or sigma.
Slow cooling or intermediate-temperature annealing permits the proposed differential diffusion and segregation.
Diffusion-driven segregation and secondary-phase formation produce a multiphase microstructure.
Rapid quenching preserves a homogeneous high-temperature BCC structure by freezing in a uniform composition.
The mechanism is expected to operate under thermal exposures above approximately 600°C where atomic mobility is sufficient.
The mechanism should not operate during low-temperature exposure or rapid quenching because diffusion is kinetically suppressed.
Relative to a rapidly quenched baseline, slowly cooled and 650°C-annealed specimens will show additional diffraction peaks indicative of secondary ordered phases.
Relative to the baseline, slowly cooled and annealed specimens will show precipitate-like microstructural features and local Cr enrichment.
The exact identity of the secondary ordered phase may be B2, sigma, or another intermetallic variant.
Local lattice distortion, chemical disparity, and possible minor-element effects influence which ordered phase forms.
The controlled comparison uses identical high-temperature BCC starting material, with rapid quenching as the baseline and slow cooling followed by 650°C annealing as the intervention.
Failure of the slowly cooled and annealed specimens to develop either secondary phases or significant compositional variation relative to the quenched baseline would falsify the proposed mechanism.
